name: Dorsal approach to the finger carpometacarpal joints
corridor: Longitudinal dorsal interval between extensor tendons centered over the injured CMC joint or joint cluster

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand pronated on a radiolucent table and fingers free for rotational assessment and fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Prepare the full hand and wrist, assess all adjacent CMC joints, and ensure PA, lateral, and oblique imaging because overlapping anatomy can conceal malalignment.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark affected metacarpal shafts and bases, neighboring CMC joints, extensor tendon paths, and planned wire exit zones.

incision.text: Use a longitudinal incision from the metacarpal base toward the proximal carpal row between extensor tendons, centered over the affected joint or between multiple involved joints.

superficial_interval.text: Protect dorsal sensory branches and longitudinal veins, identify intertendinous connections, and mobilize extensor tendons with their loose surrounding tissue radially or ulnarly.

deep_interval.text: Use the traumatic capsular rent in acute injuries or perform a limited formal capsulotomy in partially healed or chronic cases to remove blocks and restore the CMC articulation.

layers.text: Skin, dorsal sensory branches and veins, extensor tendon interval with juncturae, dorsal capsule, then metacarpal base and distal carpal row.

structures_encountered.text: Dorsal veins, radial and ulnar sensory branches, extensor tendons and juncturae, dorsal CMC capsule, metacarpal bases, and distal carpal row are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Dorsal sensory nerves, extensor tendons and intertendinous connections, CMC cartilage, and nearby deep motor or vascular structures are at risk from dissection and fixation.

danger_zones.text: Retract radial sensory branches radially and ulnar sensory branches ulnarly; enlarge exposure rather than stretching a nerve across the operative field.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid focal traction on sensory branches and preserve tendon gliding by retracting tendons with their surrounding tissue and minimizing central wire-tendon conflict.

exposure.text: Provides direct visualization of one or several dorsal CMC joints to remove interposed tissue, reduce articular fragments, and stabilize the metacarpal bases.

limitations.text: A single narrow interval may not safely expose widely separated radial and ulnar injuries, and volar pathology or neurovascular compression may require a separate approach.

extensions.text: Lengthen proximally and distally or use separate tendon-respecting windows for multiple joints rather than excessive transverse undermining.

indications.text: Use for irreducible, unstable, delayed, or multiply injured finger CMC dislocations and fracture-dislocations requiring direct reduction or fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Open exposure is unnecessary when early closed reduction is anatomic, stable, and maintainable without tendon or nerve compromise.

implant_implications.text: Place K-wires or screws to stabilize the injured ray to a stable adjacent metacarpal or carpus while avoiding central extensor-tendon tethering and articular penetration.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use true lateral plus PA and oblique views to confirm parallel CMC joint lines, restoration of metacarpal cascade, articular reduction, and safe hardware.

closure.text: Repair the capsule with nonabsorbable suture, repair any divided intertendinous connection, verify tendon glide, and close skin without nerve entrapment.

complications.text: Complications include missed residual dislocation, reduction loss, sensory neurapraxia or neuroma, extensor adhesion, stiffness, pin infection, post-traumatic arthritis, and weakness.

bailouts.text: If one incision cannot safely expose multiple joints, use an additional tendon-respecting window; if reduction remains blocked, directly identify the interposed capsule, tendon, or fracture fragment.

procedure_applications.condition: A second-through-fifth CMC dislocation or fracture-dislocation is irreducible, unstable, chronic, or blocked by interposed tissue

questions.question: What determines incision placement for multiple CMC injuries?
questions.answer: It is centered between the affected joints while respecting extensor tendons.

questions.question: Which superficial structures require protection?
questions.answer: Dorsal sensory nerve branches and longitudinal veins.

questions.question: What must be repaired if divided during exposure?
questions.answer: The dorsal capsule and any cut intertendinous connection.
